chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Al-Haysam ibn Abi Masruq al-Nehdi, from Abdul Aziz ibn Umar, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Which characteristics are most beautiful for a man?
He (peace be upon him) replied: Dignity without awe, generosity without seeking reward, and being occupied with matters other than the comforts of the world.
ai.seo_question: What are the best character traits a Muslim should cultivate according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines the spiritual aesthetics of the believer, emphasizing that true nobility lies in balanced conduct: dignity (*waqar*) that is approachable rather than intimidating, and generosity (*simaḥ*) that is purely for God’s sake. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (character) as a manifestation of inner faith, where the believer remains detached from the transient allure of *mata' al-dunya* (worldly comforts) by engaging in meaningful, higher pursuits.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-36 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Haysam ibn Abi Masruq al-Nehdi, on the authority of Abdul Aziz ibn Umar, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi, “I asked Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), ‘Which characteristics are better for a man?’
The Imam (MGB) replied, ‘Dignity without being awesome, generosity without demanding something in return, and attending to affairs other than worldly affairs.’”
